expected: Faster, more reliable indexing from the sitemap, canonical URLs and robots.txt.
Richer, page-specific previews when links are shared in Instagram DMs, Facebook, iMessage, WhatsApp, LinkedIn and X.
Clearer entity understanding of Kay Joy Flowers, her book and her services in Google and AI answer engines, from consistent Person, Book, Product and Service markup.

Live-site Lighthouse after deploy: will be measured in Phase 5.
Beacons checkout pages: blocked to automated visitors (Cloudflare), so they need a manual click-through.
Stripe payment link prices: the connected Stripe account isn't the one that holds the scan links, so prices couldn't be read by API. The links return HTTP 200.
lighthouse_note: Before and after were both measured on the same local copy of GitHub Pages (Lighthouse 12, mobile, simulated throttling, median of 3), so the comparison is like for like. Absolute timings differ slightly from the live site, which was 1.80–1.86 s LCP (Library 3.50 s) on 17 November. One trade-off: on Fearlessly Unfuckwithable the cover image now loads eagerly and becomes the largest element, so median LCP moved from 1.45 s (headline text) to 1.65 s (image). The page doesn't paint any later, and the score stays 99–100. Page weight counts uncompressed text on the local server; GitHub Pages compresses it.

deployment_detail: Not deployed. As instructed, nothing has been merged into main, so the live site is unchanged. GitHub Pages deploys from main with its built-in 'pages build and deployment' workflow; merging the branch is the whole deployment. After Kay says "deploy", Phase 5 will merge, wait for the Pages build to finish, then check the live site: every page, metadata and JSON-LD from the deployed HTML, robots.txt and the sitemap, desktop and mobile screenshots, and live Lighthouse. Checkout destinations are checked on the live site too (Stripe automatically; Beacons by Kay's click-through).
